entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; justice.gov serves curl a bot-check interstitial). The release is titled "Attorney General Pamela Bondi Releases First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files" and dated Thursday, February 27, 2025, as press release number 25-201 ("Updated February 27, 2025"). It says the Attorney General, "in conjunction with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), declassified and publicly released files", and that DOJ "intends to release the remaining documents upon review and redaction to protect the identities of Epstein's victims".
Linked files (all on justice.gov/ag/media/<id>/dl):
- the AG's letter (1391331)
- "A. Evidence List" (1391271)

Sampled files returned HTTP 200 application/pdf, with Last-Modified dates of 28 Feb 2025.
The stated authority is declassification by the AG with the FBI. This release predates the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The Epstein Library now also lists this material as "First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files" under DOJ Disclosures (https://www.justice.gov/epstein/doj-disclosures/first-phase-declassified-epstein-files), as four EFTA-renumbered PDFs (EFTA02846457 to EFTA02846673). The original press-release attachments and the library copies could diverge, so both URLs are worth watching.
Redaction: two attachments are labelled "_Redacted". No further redaction policy is stated on the release page.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.justice.gov/legalpolicies says "Unless otherwise indicated, information on Department of Justice websites is in the public domain". That is site-wide, and the attached records were not created by DOJ itself, so their status is unverified. I did not check the contents of the attachments.

entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; curl gets a bot-check interstitial). The page has sections "Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R. 4405)", "Court Records", "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)", "Prior DOJ Disclosures" and "Related Documentation".
- EFTA section: links "Data Set 1 Files" to "Data Set 12 Files" (for example https://www.justice.gov/epstein/doj-disclosures/data-set-1-files). These are paginated lists of EFTA-numbered PDFs; Data Set 1 starts at EFTA00000001.pdf.
- Court Records: about 55 per-case pages, including United States v. Maxwell, No. 1:20-cr-00330 (S.D.N.Y.), [redacted] v. Maxwell, No. 1:15-cv-07433 (S.D.N.Y.), In re: Grand Jury 05-02 (WPB) & 07-103 (WPB), No. 9:25-mc-80920 (S.D. Fla. 2025), State of Florida v. Epstein (Fla. 15th Cir. Ct. 2006 and 2008), and CA Florida Holdings, LLC, Publisher of the Palm Beach Post v. Aronberg, No. 50-2019-CA-014681 (Fla. 15th Cir. Ct. 2019).
- FOIA: CBP, FBI, BOP and Florida.
- Prior DOJ Disclosures: "First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files", "BOP Video Footage" (MP4), "Maxwell Proffer" (WAV and PDF), and "Memoranda and Correspondence".
- Related Documentation: the Attorney Review Protocol memo (4 Jan 2026), press release 26-84, and letters to Congress dated 19 Dec 2025, 30 Jan 2026 and 14 Feb 2026.
Legal authority: Epstein Files Transparency Act, Pub. L. 119-38, 139 Stat. 656, signed 19 Nov 2025. DOJ's 19 Dec 2025 letter also cites court orders in S.D. Fla. and S.D.N.Y. authorising production of material previously under protective orders or grand-jury secrecy. Releases: 19 Dec 2025, and 30 Jan 2026 (DOJ: "nearly 3.5 million pages" in total).
Redaction policy, quoted from the page: "Redactions of victim names and other identifying information have been applied. In audio files, redactions of victim names and other identifying information have been implemented through the use of a steady, solid tone." Press release 26-84 adds that S.D.N.Y. used "an additional review protocol to ensure compliance with a Court order". The page shows no "last updated" date; the parent library page shows "Last Updated: September 11, 2026". The court-record pages are DOJ's copies, and DOJ redacts some case captions (for example "[redacted] v. Maxwell"). The court's own docket remains the canonical record for each case.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.justice.gov/legalpolicies says "Unless otherwise indicated, information on Department of Justice websites is in the public domain", with the caveat that material from other sources needs the source's permission. That is a site-wide policy, not data-specific. Not checked: per-data-set file counts or sizes, whether zipped bulk downloads exist, and the contents of individual files.

entries.title: U.S. Department of Justice Epstein Library
entries.description: The Department of Justice's public library of Epstein-related records, published under the Epstein Files Transparency Act (Pub. L. 119-38). It is the landing page and full-text search for DOJ's disclosures, and it links to the House Oversight Committee's disclosures.

access.auth_note: Age-confirmation prompt ("Are you 18 years of age or older?") before viewing; no account needed.

coverage.spatial: United States (federal investigations and prosecutions; records from New York, Florida and other jurisdictions)
coverage.temporal: not stated on the page (DOJ's 30 Jan 2026 letter describes the material as spanning "a period of over twenty years")

entries.license: unverified — mixed; DOJ-authored records are public domain per DOJ site policy, but the library also holds court filings by parties, third-party and publicly submitted material that are not US Gov works
entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Justice, Epstein Library
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; curl gets an Akamai bot-check interstitial, so reachability.headless is needed). The page is titled "Epstein Library" and says: "This site houses materials responsive under the Epstein Files Transparency Act. This site will be updated if additional documents are identified for release." It shows "Last Updated: September 11, 2026". The page has a "Search Full Epstein Library" box and links to "DOJ Disclosures, Including Disclosures Under the Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R. 4405)" (see doj-epstein-files-transparency-act-disclosures) and to "House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Disclosures" (see house-oversight-epstein-doj-records). A search caveat says portions "may not be electronically searchable or may produce unreliable search results".
Legal authority: the Epstein Files Transparency Act, cited on the page as H.R. 4405 and in DOJ's Attorney Review Protocol memo (4 Jan 2026) as "Pub. L. 119-38, 139 Stat. 656". DOJ's 19 Dec 2025 letter to Congress says it was signed on 19 Nov 2025. Release dates, per DOJ letters and press release: 19 Dec 2025 ("hundreds of thousands of pages"), and 30 Jan 2026, when DOJ published "over 3 million additional pages", including "more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images", for a total of "nearly 3.5 million pages" (press release 26-84). A Section 3 report to Congress followed on 14 Feb 2026. DOJ also says the review process involved court orders unsealing grand-jury and protected material in S.D. Fla. and S.D.N.Y.
Redaction policy, quoted from the page: "all reasonable efforts have been made to review and redact personal information pertaining to victims, other private individuals, and protect sensitive materials from disclosure ... this website may nevertheless contain information that inadvertently includes non-public personally identifiable information". Errors are reported to EFTA@usdoj.gov. The 19 Dec 2025 letter lists the Act's withholding categories: victim PII, CSAM, active investigations, depictions of death or injury, and classified information. Because DOJ says it will correct inadvertent disclosures, files may be re-redacted or withdrawn in place.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.justice.gov/legalpolicies says "Unless otherwise indicated, information on Department of Justice websites is in the public domain" but also "If a source other than the Department of Justice or other federal government agency is indicated ... permission to copy these materials must be obtained from the original source." This is a site-wide policy, not a data-specific licence, and much of the library is non-DOJ material. Bulk download, total file count and per-file formats beyond the PDF, MP4 and WAV files I saw were not checked.

entries.title: DOJ OPR: Executive Summary of Report on the S.D. Fla. Resolution of Its 2006-2008 Epstein Investigation (November 2020)
entries.description: The public executive summary of the DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility's investigation into the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida's resolution of its 2006-2008 federal criminal investigation of Jeffrey Epstein, including the 2007 non-prosecution agreement, and the office's interactions with victims.

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Professional Responsibility, Executive Summary of Report (November 2020)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 application/pdf, 289,140 bytes, Last-Modified "Thu, 12 Nov 2020" (headless Chromium session; justice.gov serves curl a bot-check page). The old /download URL redirects to /dl?inline=. The PDF is 13 pages, headed "EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF REPORT ... Investigation into the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida's Resolution of Its 2006-2008 Federal Criminal Investigation of Jeffrey Epstein and Its Interactions with Victims during the Investigation ... November 2020".
Release: 12 Nov 2020. DOJ's statement of that date (https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/statement-doj-office-professional-responsibility-report-jeffrey-epstein-2006-2008, press release 20-1227, "Updated February 5, 2025") says the executive summary "was released today to affected victims" and is on the DOJ website. Redaction: the summary names the then-U.S. Attorney, but no victims. No separate redaction statement is shown. Court-filed copies of OPR material also appear in DOJ's Epstein Library under United States v. Maxwell, No. 1:20-cr-00330; those were not checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: DOJ-authored, and https://www.justice.gov/legalpolicies says "Unless otherwise indicated, information on Department of Justice websites is in the public domain". High confidence.

entries.title: U.S. Sentencing Commission Datafiles
entries.description: The Sentencing Commission's annual case-level datafiles on sentences imposed in federal criminal cases — individual offenders, organizational defendants, and special collections — with identifiers removed, for quantitative research on federal sentencing.
entries.attribution: United States Sentencing Commission, Commission Datafiles
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes the datafiles as excluding identifiers and providing "fiscal year data for researchers interested in studying federal sentencing practices". It lists Individuals, Organizations, Special Collections, and Special Reports datafiles, and says they are also distributed through ICPSR. The SAS/SPSS formats come from the Commission's usual distribution and were not checked file by file. The USSC is an independent agency in the judicial branch.
